label: D1 after a rewarded trial, when the policy is not leaning strongly toward a2 (a1-biased reward signal)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), and almost only when the reward input is 1: rewarded D1 steps hold 97.7% of activation mass, but only 41% of them activate. The rest is set by the model leaning toward a1. It fires mostly after a1 choices (prev_action=1 rate 0.157 vs 0.041 for a2), when S1 is the hidden good state, and when the D1 policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) is above about -1.5. It is silent during long rewarded a2 streaks. The top activations are rewards that come after a1 choices that went unrewarded. It does NOT fire on unrewarded D1s (1% rate), penalty trials, or any GO or D2 step. It is stronger early in the episode (ep_trial 3-9) and fades by trials 90-99, and it is concentrated in the mid value bin (7.54-7.73). Dev scores: reward-at-D1 alone F1 0.57 (recall 0.92, mass recall 0.98); adding prev_action==1 gives F1 0.59; adding the policy-logit condition gives F1 0.71 (mass recall 0.96). I recorded the logit version. It uses only observed inputs plus the model's own policy readout, so no future variables.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 8 (9 = most a1) (+6.15), choice_bin=decile 8 (9 = most a1) (+4.55), phase=D1 & last=a1 S2 r (+4.06), in_rew=1 (+3.68), phase=D1 & before=a1 S2 r (+3.13), phase=D1 & before=a1 S2 u (+3.03). Lower it: in_rew=0 (-5.99), before=a2 S1 u (-2.76), choice_bin=decile 3 (9 = most a1) (-2.21), before=a1 S1 u (-2.21).
